quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only after a crash.
After a crash or when stopped for a ticket.
Only when stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a crash or when stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance when you drive. Show it to a police officer along with your license whenever asked after a traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather so you can see ahead.
Farther back than you would behind a regular car.
One car length behind the truck so the driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close to a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Tailgating is dangerous because you lose time to stop if the truck brakes suddenly.

questions.question: What blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes (rubbernecking) causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you go in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the right lane, even if other lights show red. Always let pedestrians and cars in the intersection go first.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots. The driver cannot see your car behind them or to the left of the cab. If you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another car?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to return.
When you look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when there is a safe gap between your car and the car you passed. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back.

questions.question: If you park in an unusual spot, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your car from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked car must not be a hazard. Always park where drivers approaching from any direction can see it.

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Push your head back against the headrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing back into your seat and pushing your head against the headrest. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another car.

questions.question: As vehicle speed increases, what happens to stopping distance and crash severity?

options.text: They decrease.
They stay the same.
They increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you do not think about it.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the interstate to calm down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your driving. If you are angry, upset, afraid, or worried, wait until you feel calm before driving. You need to focus on the road.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: Construction zone signs have an orange background with black letters. They appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides on divided highways.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use the side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Even with all your mirrors, you have blind spots you cannot see. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check these areas.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection if no cars are coming.
Anywhere signs or road markings allow passing.
On a curve if no cars are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anywhere signs or road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lots, or alleys. If a curve or hill blocks your view, do not pass—another car might be coming. Only pass where signs or markings permit it and you have enough space.

questions.question: Is backing up your vehicle dangerous?

options.text: Yes, always.
Only if someone is helping you.
Only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, always.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Use extra caution.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beams.
Parking lights.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: In Arizona, vehicles must have liability insurance:

options.text: Only when driven on an interstate.
At all times.
Only when driven by a minor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Every vehicle in Arizona must have liability insurance. The policy must be from Arizona and cover where you mainly drive.

questions.question: To make a right turn correctly, you should:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before you turn. Slow down and use the right lane. Stay close to the right curb or edge of the road.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not go until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.
Under no circumstances.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull off the road.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead, like a change in road direction, a steep hill, or another hazard.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Turn only when the intersection is clear and the signal allows.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Ease up on the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease up on the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Release the gas or brake pedal to regain control. Steer in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is caused by going too fast on wet roads. Slow down on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection:

options.text: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: With a green light, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection. Drivers must yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and look both ways. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a broken white line marking:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross a broken white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you may:

options.text: Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.
Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.
